question: The One Health framework recognises that emerging infectious diseases like Nipah and COVID-19 can be adequately controlled by focusing exclusively on human vaccination and treatment, without monitoring animal populations or ecosystems.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. The One Health framework is built on the principle that human health cannot be protected in isolation. Emerging infections arise at the human-animal-environment interface — effective prevention requires integrated surveillance of wildlife reservoirs, ecological disruption and zoonotic spillover pathways, not human-focused measures alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. The One Health framework explicitly recognises that human, animal and environmental health are interconnected. Nipah (bat reservoir, pig amplifier host), COVID-19 (suspected zoonotic spillover) and H5N1 (avian reservoirs) demonstrate that controlling EIDs requires integrated surveillance across human, animal and ecological domains.
